title: Foreign Exchange Rates - H.10 - April 20, 2026
summary: The Federal Reserve released weekly H.10 foreign exchange rate data for April 13-17, 2026, showing USD exchange rates against 20 currencies. Key rates included EUR/USD at 1.1801, USD/JPY at 158.10, USD/GBP at 1.3556, and USD/CNY at 6.817. The Broad Dollar Index declined from 118.99 to 118.08 over the period, while the AFE Index fell from 111.47 to 110.46 and the EME Index dropped from 128.41 to 127.61. This is reference data with no accompanying Fed commentary.
key_points: USD/EUR ranged 1.1710-1.1801, ending the week at 1.1801 (weaker dollar vs prior week)
Broad Dollar Index declined from 118.99 to 118.08 over the tracking week
Emerging Market Dollar Index (EME) dropped from 128.41 to 127.61
Advanced Foreign Economy Index (AFE) fell from 111.47 to 110.46
why_it_matters: The H.10 release provides the official Federal Reserve measure of trade-weighted dollar indices used widely in policy and research contexts. However, this specific release contains only numerical data with no Fed commentary on currency dynamics, policy signals, or market implications. Its archival value is as reference data for historical analysis rather than as an active market catalyst.
macro_context: The H.10 data shows the U.S. dollar weakening modestly against major currencies during the week of April 13-17, 2026. The broad index declined approximately 0.77% and the EME index fell approximately 0.63%, suggesting broad-based dollar softness. This release is pure reference data without any Fed commentary, policy signals, or interpretive context.
